_note: Curated set of words where Saadia's tafsir uses a sense distinct from standard classical Arabic. Each entry contrasts the classical Lane meaning with the sense Saadia is reaching for, and names the mechanism (calque, philosophical gloss, anti-anthropomorphism, coinage). The `sources` array per entry lists honestly what informed the gloss. Blau's Dictionary and his Festschrift article on Genesis 1-12 are cited only where they genuinely back the present claim; entries that are our own reading of the Saadia text against Lane say so. This project is dedicated to the memory of Yehoshua Blau ז״ל (1919-2020), whose lexicographical work made readings like these possible. See /about/blau.

_sources.lane: Lane's Lexicon (E.W. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, 1863-93; Perseus TEI edition via ~/Tools/arabic-lexicon)
_sources.saadia-direct: Direct reading of Saadia's Tafsir as printed in data/tafsir-bereshit-{N}.json (Cairo 2019 edition)
_sources.blau-dict: Yehoshua Blau, A Dictionary of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts (Jerusalem: Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, 2006). Cited per entry where the dictionary entry genuinely bears on the present gloss.
_sources.blau-festschrift: Yehoshua Blau, 'עיונים בתרגום רב סעדיה גאון לבראשית פרקים א-יב', in Sefer Zikaron le-Rav Yosef ben David Qafiḥ z"l, pp. 309-318. Cited only when a Festschrift note treats the same verse, with the relation (direct, same-verse-different-lexeme, or parallel-pattern) made explicit.

_scope: Bereshit 1-11 + three demos from later books (Bamidbar, Devarim) showing Saadia-specific senses with direct Blau backing

entries.classical_en: covering, overwhelming (esp. of deep water)
entries.classical_he: מציף, מכסה (בדרך כלל לתיאור מים עמוקים)
entries.saadia_en: submerged, flooded — used to render תֹהוּ ("chaos / formless")
entries.mechanism: interpretive: Saadia reads primordial chaos as primordial water, not nothingness

blau_dict.sense: abyss / תהום (Blau attests غمر as a JA noun meaning "abyss", citing Saadia on Tehillim 129:7)

entries.classical_en: Form X of بحر "sea" — extremely rare in classical Arabic, mostly poetic for "to become vast as a sea"
entries.classical_he: בנין מקביל ל'התפעל' מן השורש בח"ר ("ים") — נדיר בקלאסי, בעיקר בשירה במשמעות "להיות עצום כים"
entries.saadia_en: vast like a sea — used to render בֹהוּ ("void")
entries.mechanism: Saadianic coinage — pairs with גאמרה (Gen 1:2) to make תהו ובהו = "flooded and sea-like"

blau_dict.sense: Form X استبحر "to be covered by water, to overflow / לְהִיוֹת מְכֻסֶּה בַּמַּיִם, לְהִיוֹת מוּצָף" — Blau attests Form X explicitly citing Saadia (לבראשית, the creation account) for exactly the participial form Saadia uses to render בֹּהוּ at Gen 1:2.

entries.classical_en: winds (plural of رِيح); also: spirit, breath
entries.classical_he: רוחות (רבים של רִיח); גם: רוח, נשמה
entries.saadia_en: winds (plural) — Saadia translates רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים as "winds of God," not "spirit of God"
entries.saadia_he: רוחות (בלשון רבים) — מתרגם "רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים" כ"רוחות של ה'"
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic: a literal wind rather than a divine "spirit" hovering over the waters

entries.classical_en: to blow (of wind)
entries.classical_he: לנשוב (לרוח)
entries.saadia_en: blows — used to render מְרַחֶפֶת ("hovering") over the waters
entries.mechanism: interpretive: pairs with ריאח above — the literal wind "blows," not a spirit "hovers"

entries.classical_en: to will, to wish
entries.classical_he: לרצות, לחפוץ
entries.saadia_en: willed — Saadia consistently renders Hebrew וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים as "God willed," not "God said"
entries.saadia_he: רצה — סעדיה מתרגם בעקביות "וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים" כ"רצה ה'", לא "אמר ה'"
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic: divine creation is by will, not by speech-act

blau_dict.sense: Form I (classical): to want / רצה (post-classical usage shows weakening of the volition sense in conjunctions; Blau collects the JA-attested idioms)

entries.classical_en: hard skin, hide; hardness, firmness
entries.classical_he: עור קשה, חוסן
entries.saadia_en: firmament, expanse — Saadia's standard rendering of רָקִיעַ
entries.saadia_he: רקיע, מרחב — תרגומו הקבוע של סעדיה ל"רָקִיעַ"
entries.mechanism: loanshift / semantic calque on Hebrew רקיע — Saadia takes the classical sense of "hardness" and stretches it to cover the celestial dome

blau_dict.sense: Blau's JA Dictionary records جلد as a verb "to bear calmly, to endure" (different semantic field); the firmament-sense calque from Saadia is our own observation against Lane

entries.classical_en: given authority over, set in dominion
entries.classical_he: מוצב לשררה, ניתנה לו סמכות
entries.saadia_en: ruling, given dominion — Saadia inserts מסלטא as an explanatory gloss on בְּצַלְמֵנוּ ("in our image") — the "image" of God is dominion, not visual likeness; the same word later glosses husband-over-wife (3:16) and Cain-over-sin (4:7) as functional rule, not raw force
entries.saadia_he: שליט, ניתנה לו ממשלה — סעדיה מוסיף את "מסלטא" כפירוש ל"בְּצַלְמֵנוּ" — ה"צלם" הוא השליטה, לא הדמיון החזותי; אותה לשון חוזרת על שליטת הבעל באשה (ג טז) ועל שליטת קין בחטא (ד ז) — שלטון כתפקיד, לא ככוח גרידא
entries.mechanism: Anti-anthropomorphic theological gloss extended into a programmatic dominion-vocabulary system, now confirmed across TWO books and three semantic registers (divine-dominion-grant + human-vicegerency + legal-authority). Saadia uses the Form II passive participle مسلَّط ('one set in authority over, made-dominant') and its Form V cognate تسلَّط ('to gain mastery, to have legal authority') as the invariant Pentateuchal vocabulary for the dominion semantic field. The cross-register arc: (1) the imago-Dei theological core — Heb צֶלֶם is read NOT as visual-resemblance but as FUNCTIONAL DOMINION (man set-as-master over creation) at Gen 1:26, 1:27, 5:1; the cognate sin-mastery voluntarist account at Gen 4:7 ('sin couches at the door...you shall rule over it' = יתסלט בה / שאלת תתסלט בה); the post-flood resumption of dominion at Gen 9:6; the Edenic gender-hierarchy of Gen 3:16 ('he shall rule over you' = יתסלט עליך); (2) the human-vicegerency extension at Gen 24:2 ('Abraham's senior servant set over all his property' = אלמסלט עלי' גמיע מאלה — same Form II passive participle for the steward as for the imago-Dei vicegerent); (3) the Mosaic divine-sovereignty assertion at Ex 8:18 ('that you may know I am God in the midst of the earth' = אני אללה מסלט עלי' גמיע אלעאלם — Saadia interpolates مسلَّط to make explicit what בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ implies: active sovereign presence-as-dominion); (4) the legal-authority extension at Ex 21:8 (Heb לֹא יִמְשֹׁל לְמָכְרָהּ 'he has no power to sell her' = לא יתסלט אן יביעהא — Form V deployed for human-legal-authority). The cross-book consistency confirms that مسلَّط/تسلَّط is Saadia's systematic Arabic terminus-technicus for the entire Heb מָשַׁל-dominion vocabulary, applied invariantly whether the dominion is bestowed by God on man (imago-Dei), by man on man (steward over property; husband over wife), exercised by God himself (sovereign over the earth), or claimed by humans in legal contexts (authority over a betrothed slave-woman). The systematic anti-anthropomorphic-and-lexical-fixity makes this one of Saadia's most consistent translational programs. Pedagogically distinctive because the cross-register breadth surfaces the entry's real shape: not an isolated anti-anthropomorphic move at the imago-Dei verses but a programmatic dominion-vocabulary spanning theology, household-economy, divine-sovereignty, and legal-authority — all carried by a single Arabic Form II/V pair.

blau_dict.sense: Form V + على (post-classical): to gain mastery over / השתלט; with the idiom تسلط على = השתלט על. Blau cites Yefet on Habakkuk 3:8 ('the first enemy who gained mastery over Israel') — same construction Saadia uses in Gen 4:7. The R2 cross-book scan confirms that Saadia deploys the Form II passive participle مسلَّط and its Form V cognate consistently across Bereshit (the imago-Dei + Cain + Eve + Noahide-dominion verses at 1:26, 1:27, 3:16, 4:7, 5:1, 9:6 + the household-steward verse at 24:2) and Shemot (the divine-sovereignty assertion at 8:18 + the legal-authority verse at 21:8), making the dominion-vocabulary a 2-book program.

entries.classical_en: to disable, to render inactive, to suspend (a thing's function)
entries.classical_he: להשבית, להפסיק תפקודו של דבר
entries.saadia_en: ceased, desisted — Saadia uses عطّل to render וַיִּשְׁבֹּת ("He rested"); God did not rest (which implies fatigue), He ceased acting
entries.saadia_he: חדל, השבית — סעדיה מתרגם "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת" ב"עטל"; ה' לא נח (שכן הדבר משתמע מעייפות), אלא חדל לפעול
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic: divine "rest" is reframed as cessation of activity

blau_dict.sense: Blau's JA entry attests عطل as a noun for "economic depression / התמוטטות, שפל וקיפאון במסחר" (Pirqei Avot commentary) — a JA-specific commercial sense. Saadia's use here is the classical Form II "to render inactive" that Lane records, not the JA commercial register.

entries.classical_en: speaking, articulate; (in philosophy) rational
entries.classical_he: מדבר, מבטא; (בפילוסופיה) רציונלי
entries.saadia_en: rational — Saadia translates נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה ("living soul") as נפס נאטקה, "rational soul" — the Aristotelian/Galenic technical term for the human soul as distinct from the animal soul; he restricts the term to Adam (2:7) and uses it again in 3:20 to gloss "mother of all living" as "mother of every rational living being"
entries.saadia_he: רציונלית — סעדיה מתרגם "נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" כ"נפס נאטקה", "נפש מדברת/הוגה" — מונח אריסטוטלי/גאלני לנפש האנושית בניגוד לנפש הבהמית; הוא משמר את המונח לאדם (ב ז) ומשתמש בו שוב בג כ כדי לגלוס "אם כל חי" כ"אם כל חי הוגה"
entries.mechanism: philosophical gloss: Adam's "living soul" is upgraded to the rational soul of Greek/Arabic psychology; the same restriction reappears in 3:20

blau_dict.sense: Blau records the basic Form I + بـ "to speak, to utter" and Form IV "to utter" — the JA Dictionary does not reach the philosophical "rational" sense which derives from the Greek-Arabic philosophical tradition (al-nafs al-nāṭiqa)

entries.classical_en: angels (plural of مَلاك / مَلَك)
entries.classical_he: מלאכים (רבים של מַלְאָךְ)
entries.saadia_en: angels — Saadia renders the serpent's promise וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים ("you shall be like God") as "you shall be like the angels," downgrading the comparison from divine to angelic status; same substitution in 3:24 where the keruvim are simply ملائكة
entries.saadia_he: מלאכים — סעדיה מתרגם את הבטחת הנחש "וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים" כ"תהיו כמלאכים", מוריד את ההשוואה מאלוהית לאנגלית; אותו חילוף מופיע בג כד כאשר הכרובים הם פשוט ملائكة
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic: Hebrew אֱלֹהִים referring to lesser divine beings (or the serpent's promise of divinity) is rerouted to "angels," closing off any path to creaturely apotheosis

blau_dict.sense: Blau treats ملكوتي ("characteristic of angels") under root ملك, citing the Kuzari — adjacent to the angelic semantic field but not the lemma ملائكة directly

entries.classical_en: Form IV of طغى "to transgress, exceed bounds" — caused me to transgress
entries.classical_he: בנין הפעיל מן השורש ط-غ-ي ("לחרוג, לעבור גבול") — גרם לי לחרוג
entries.saadia_en: led me astray, seduced me — Saadia renders Eve's הִשִּׁיאַנִי ("deceived me") with the strong moral-transgression vocabulary of طغى rather than the neutral خدع ("deceived")
entries.saadia_he: הדיח אותי, פיתה אותי — סעדיה מתרגם את "הִשִּׁיאַנִי" של חוה בלשון העבירה המוסרית החריפה של طغى, ולא בפועל הניטרלי خدع ("רימה")
entries.mechanism: interpretive: deception is recast as moral transgression — the serpent did not merely trick Eve, he caused her to overstep a divine boundary; Form IV transfers the agency of the sin to the serpent

entries.classical_en: Form II active participle of قرّ — "declaring, affirming, establishing as fact"
entries.classical_he: בינוני פועל של בנין פיעל מן ق-ر-ر — "מצהיר, מאשר, קובע כעובדה"
entries.saadia_en: by way of confirmation — Saadia inserts مقرِّرًا as an adverbial gloss on God's rhetorical questions ("Where are you?" 3:9; "Where is your brother?" 4:9), signaling that God is not actually asking — He is confronting
entries.saadia_he: בלשון פסקנית / מצהירה — סעדיה מוסיף "מקררא" כתואר-פועל לשאלותיו הרטוריות של ה' ("איך אנת" ג ט; "אין הבל אכ'אך" ד ט), כדי לרמוז שאין כאן שאלה אמיתית — אלא עימות
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic insertion: God's questions in the garden and after Cain's murder are not real inquiries (which would imply divine ignorance) but rhetorical confrontations

blau_dict.sense: Blau records numerous forms (I "to deposit", II "to put", IV "to leave", V "to give rest", X "to be fixed/decided") — the JA Dictionary attests the root but not the active-participle "declaratively" sense Saadia uses here

entries.classical_en: your leading-rope, your being-led; by extension, your guidance/control
entries.classical_he: החבל המוליך אותך, היותך מובלת; ובהשאלה: הנהגתך, השליטה בך
entries.saadia_en: your being-led — Saadia translates Eve's תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ ("your desire," for her husband) as "your being-led-by your husband," and uses the same noun in 4:7 for sin's relation to Cain ("to you is its leading")
entries.saadia_he: היותך מובלת — סעדיה מתרגם את "תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ" של חוה (אל בעלה) כ"היותך מובלת על ידי בעלך", ומשתמש באותו שם-עצם בד ז עבור יחס החטא לקין ("ואליך קיאדה")
entries.mechanism: interpretive: the erotic Hebrew תְּשׁוּקָה is desexualized into a vocabulary of leading/submission; the same noun then keys 4:7's paired gloss — sin pulls Cain, but Cain (مسلَّط بالإختيار) masters it

blau_dict.sense: Form I + إلى: "to lead, to cause, to effect, to bring about / להביא לעשות" (metaphorical, used of agency); Form VII: "to obey, to yield to / נשמע, נכנע לו". Blau cites Maimonides' Guide of the Perplexed I (Munk/Joel/Kafih).

blau_festschrift.note: Blau's Festschrift note on Gen 3:16 treats עצב/עצבון → משקה ("effort/toil") and corrects Kapach's lexical distinction. The present entry on תשוקה → قياد is independent — Blau does not discuss this lexeme in the article.

entries.classical_en: body, torso; tunic worn directly on the body
entries.classical_he: גוף, גזע הגוף; כותונת הנלבשת על הגוף
entries.saadia_en: body — Saadia renders כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר ("garments of skin") as ת'יאב בדן ("body-garments"), conspicuously avoiding the literal جلد ("skin/hide") — the same root he reserves for "firmament"
entries.saadia_he: גוף — סעדיה מתרגם "כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר" כ"ת'יאב בדן" ("בגדי גוף"), ונמנע במכוון מן המילה جلد ("עור"), שאת אותו שורש ייעד לרקיע
entries.mechanism: interpretive: the literal "animal skins" is muted — possibly to dodge the implication that God slaughtered animals for clothing, possibly to keep جلد reserved for רָקִיעַ. Either way, the divergence from the obvious lexical choice is deliberate

blau_dict.sense: "clothing without sleeves, item / בגד ללא שרוולים" — Blau records بدن in JA as a textile term (Dozy; Gil, Eretz Yisrael, II:145), confirming that for Saadia's audience ت'יאב بدن had a specific clothing-register sense, not just generic "body-garment"

entries.classical_en: your error, your mistake (light moral weight in classical usage; خطيئة is the heavier "sin")
entries.classical_he: טעותך, שגיאתך (משקל מוסרי קל בשימוש הקלאסי; خطيئة היא "החטא" החמור)
entries.saadia_en: your error — Saadia uses خطأ ("error") rather than the heavier خطيئة ("sin") to render Hebrew חַטָּאת in God's warning to Cain ("sin crouches at the door"), softening the categorical weight of the term
entries.saadia_he: טעותך — סעדיה משתמש ב-خطأ ("שגיאה") במקום במונח החמור יותר خطيئة ("חטא") לתרגום "חַטָּאת" באזהרת ה' לקין ("חטאת רובץ"), ומקל את משקלה הקטגורי של המילה
entries.mechanism: interpretive: in the Kalam ethical lexicon خطأ vs خطيئة tracks inadvertence vs deliberation; Saadia's choice of the lighter term sets up the immediately following voluntarist gloss ("and you are the master over it by choice") — moral failure is something the agent can master, not an ontological category

blau_dict.sense: Blau attests Form II "to induce to sin / החטיאו, הביאו לידי חטא" (citing Yefet on Pirqei Avot) and Form IV + على "doubtfully, without knowing whether one is right" (Geniza letter, Goitein). The JA Dictionary thus distinguishes the inducement and uncertainty senses — adjacent to but not the same as our contrast between خطأ and خطيئة.

entries.classical_en: choice, election, selection
entries.classical_he: בחירה, ברירה
entries.saadia_en: free choice (libertarian sense) — Saadia inserts بِالإِخْتِيَارِ ("by free choice") into God's address to Cain, making the mastery over sin explicitly a matter of free will — the Mu'tazilite technical term for the libertarian view that humans are causally autonomous moral agents
entries.saadia_he: בחירה חופשית (במובן הליברטריאני) — סעדיה מכניס "באלאכ'תיאר" ("מתוך בחירה חופשית") לדברי ה' אל קין, ועושה את השליטה בחטא לעניין של בחירה חופשית במפורש — המונח הטכני המועתזלי לעמדה שהאדם הוא סוכן מוסרי אוטונומי
entries.mechanism: philosophical gloss / theological insertion: Saadia smuggles his (and the Mu'tazilites') libertarian voluntarism into the text — the very word اختيار is the Kalam shibboleth for free will against predetermination

blau_dict.sense: Form VIII: "to choose / בחר" (also negation), and Form X: "to decide by divination, to leave the choice to God / השאיר את הבחירה בידי האלוהים של ניחוש." Blau attests the choice-semantic field but the Mu'tazilite kalam reading of اختيار as libertarian free will is a separate philosophical context.

entries.classical_en: Form III of قال — to engage in dialogue, to dispute, to converse back-and-forth (reciprocal action)
entries.classical_he: בנין שלישי של ق-و-ل — לנהל דו-שיח, להתווכח, לדבר הדדית
entries.saadia_en: disputed with — Saadia renders the famously elliptical וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל-הֶבֶל ("and Cain said to Abel..." with no content given) by upgrading the verb to Form III قاوَلَ ("he disputed/argued with him"), filling the textual gap with an argument rather than mere speech
entries.saadia_he: התווכח — סעדיה מתרגם את "וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל-הֶבֶל" הסתום (שאין בו תוכן דיבור) בכך שהוא מעלה את הפועל לבניין השלישי قاوَلَ ("הוא התווכח אתו"), וממלא את הפער הטקסטואלי בריב במקום בדיבור גרידא
entries.mechanism: interpretive: where the Hebrew leaves an aposiopesis (Cain spoke — but what?), Saadia commits to "they argued," pre-empting the murder with a verbal quarrel; the choice of Form III over the simple قال is the lexical fingerprint of this reading

blau_dict.sense: Form III: "to make a contract, to make a covenant with / כרית עמו" AND "to quarrel with, to argue / נשפט עמו, דבר עמו." Blau's JA Dictionary directly attests the "to quarrel/argue" sense of قاول that the present entry depends on — strong corroboration that Saadia's listeners would have heard 'disputed' here, not 'spoke'.

entries.classical_en: obedience, submission, willing compliance
entries.classical_he: ציות, היענות, כניעה ברצון
entries.saadia_en: obedience — Saadia renders וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ ... אֶת-הָאֱלֹהִים ("walked with God") as סלך פי טאעה' אללה ("walked in obedience to God") for both Enoch (5:22, 5:24) and Noah (6:9), abstracting the relational/spatial Hebrew image into an ethical category
entries.saadia_he: ציות — סעדיה מתרגם את "וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ ... אֶת-הָאֱלֹהִים" כ"סלך פי טאעה' אללה" ("הלך בציות לה'"), הן על חנוך (ה כב, ה כד) והן על נוח (ו ט), ומפשט את התמונה היחסית-מרחבית של העברית לקטגוריה מוסרית
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic: the intimate Hebrew picture of "walking with God" — which seems to put Enoch in God's presence — is recast as the abstract category of religious obedience

blau_dict.sense: Blau treats Form X (classical) "to be able, to have power to do something" with the note that this is influenced by qadar (divine decree). The Dictionary engages the root in the kalam-philosophical register but not the noun طاعة specifically.

entries.classical_en: Form V passive — "his (allotted lifespan) was completed"; standard classical Arabic euphemism for "he died"
entries.classical_he: בניין התפעל סביל — "הושלם (חייו המוקצים לו)"; שם-לוואי קלאסי סטנדרטי למוות
entries.saadia_en: he died — where the Hebrew has the famously ambiguous וְאֵינֶנּוּ כִּי-לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים ("and he was no more, for God took him"), Saadia inserts תופי ("he died") before "and God took him," closing off any reading on which Enoch was assumed alive
entries.saadia_he: נפטר — במקום שהעברית מותירה את הניסוח הסתום "וְאֵינֶנּוּ כִּי-לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים", סעדיה מוסיף "תופי" ("נפטר") לפני "וקבצ'ה אללה", וסוגר כל קריאה שלפיה חנוך נלקח חי
entries.mechanism: anti-mystical insertion: the apocryphal-mystical reading of Enoch's assumption (Jub. 4, 1 En., later Hekhalot traditions) is foreclosed by inserting a plain "he died" — Enoch was a righteous man who died early, not a translated one

blau_dict.sense: Form VII: "to die / נפטר" — Blau attests the death-euphemism sense directly in his JA Dictionary, confirming that Saadia's audience would have heard تُوُفِّيَ as the standard idiom for "died," not a euphemism requiring interpretation.

entries.classical_en: nobles, men of high rank (plural of شريف)
entries.classical_he: אצילים, בני מעלה (רבים של شريف)
entries.saadia_en: the nobles — Saadia renders בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים ("sons of God / sons of the divine beings") as בני אלאשראף ("sons of the nobility"), paired with בנאת אלעאמה ("daughters of the common folk") for בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם — a class-based reading of the cross-caste unions that produced the Nephilim
entries.saadia_he: האצילים — סעדיה מתרגם "בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים" ("בני האלים") כ"בני אלאשראף" ("בני האצילים"), במקביל ל"בנאת אלעאמה" ("בנות פשוטי העם") לתרגום "בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם" — קריאה מעמדית של הזיווגים שהולידו את הנפילים
entries.mechanism: anti-mythological + anti-anthropomorphic: refuses both the angelic-being reading and any plain rendering that would name plural "sons of God"; the verse is reduced to a social-stratification scandal — aristocrats coercing the daughters of commoners — which also explains the moral indictment in verses 5-7

entries.classical_en: Form VII of جمد — "to be frozen / congealed / made to stagnate"
entries.classical_he: בנין VII של ج-م-د — "להיקפא, להקרש, להיעצר במקום"
entries.saadia_en: be frozen / be retained — Saadia renders the famously opaque לֹא-יָדוֹן רוּחִי בָאָדָם לְעֹלָם ("My spirit shall not contend / abide in man forever") as לא ינג'מד רוחי פי הולאי אלנאס אלי' אלדהר ("My spirit shall not be frozen in these people forever"), reading יָדוֹן as a verb of permanent retention ("abide"), not legal contention ("judge")
entries.saadia_he: תיקפא, תיעצר במקום — סעדיה מתרגם את "לֹא-יָדוֹן רוּחִי בָאָדָם לְעֹלָם" הסתום כ"לא ינג'מד רוחי פי הולאי אלנאס אלי' אלדהר" ("לא תיקפא רוחי באנשים הללו לעולם"), וקורא את הפועל יָדוֹן כפועל של החזקה קבועה ("שכן, היה אצור"), לא של ריב משפטי ("דן")
entries.mechanism: interpretive lexical choice: the Hebrew root ד-י-ן is ambiguous between "judge/contend" and "abide"; Saadia picks the abide-sense via ج-م-د ("be congealed"), turning the verse into a statement that human life-spans will no longer be indefinitely prolonged — directly setting up the 120-year limit in the same verse

blau_dict.sense: Form I: "to congeal, to stiffen / קפא, קרש, נקרש" — Blau attests the congealing sense as the basic JA usage of the root, and additionally records Form VII (تنجمد / ינג'מד) "to stiffen, to freeze, to congeal" — exactly the form Saadia uses here.

entries.classical_en: Form III/VI of وعد — to make a mutual appointment with, to set a deadline / threat against; in prophetic-Geonic usage, "to warn of impending judgment, to decree against"
entries.classical_he: בנין III/VI של ו-ע-ד — לקבוע מועד עם, להציב איום הדדי; בלשון נביאים-גאונים: "להתרות בפורענות, לגזור על"
entries.saadia_en: warned / decreed against — Saadia renders the deeply anthropomorphic וַיִּנָּחֶם יְהוָה כִּי-עָשָׂה אֶת-הָאָדָם ("and the LORD regretted that He had made man") as פתואעדהם אללה כמא צנעהם ("so God warned them as He had made them"), and similarly in 6:7 — eliminating divine regret entirely
entries.saadia_he: התרה, גזר על — סעדיה מתרגם את "וַיִּנָּחֶם יְהוָה כִּי-עָשָׂה אֶת-הָאָדָם" האנתרופומורפי במובהק כ"פתואעדהם אללה כמא צנעהם" ("וְהִתְרָה בהם ה' כפי שיצרם"), וכן בפסוק ז — וביטל את היסוד של חרטה אלוהית לחלוטין
entries.mechanism: Anti-anthropomorphic: divine regret/change-of-mind replaced by prophetic warning, now extended to the divine-restraint frame at the Abimelech-wombs passage. The Form-III/IV verb وَاعَدَ ('to warn / threaten / decree-doom against') routes biblical expressions of divine affect (Gen 6:6-7 וַיִּנָּחֶם 'and He regretted') AND of divine direct biological-action (Gen 20:18 עָצֹר עָצַר ה' בְּעַד כָּל-רֶחֶם 'God had certainly closed every womb') through the same prophetic-warning frame. The cross-narrative arc within Bereshit: (1) the flood-decision anti-anthropomorphic anchor at Gen 6:6, 6:7 (Heb וַיִּנָּחֶם 'and YHWH regretted' → תואעדהם, with the prose-prophetic frame implying the 120-year limit at Gen 6:3 functioned as a probationary warning — God did not change His mind on Yom Six, He had already announced the deadline); (2) NOW ALSO Gen 20:18 (Heb 'for YHWH had certainly restrained every womb of Abimelech's house for the matter of Sarah Abraham's wife' = לאן אללה כאן קד תואעד בחבס כל רחם לבית אבימלך — 'for God had THREATENED with the closing-up of every womb'). The Gen 20:18 attestation broadens the mechanism beyond the affective-regret category to include the direct-biological-intervention category: where the Hebrew has God directly closing wombs (an act that would imply mechanical-divine-interference in human biology), Saadia mediates this through the same prophetic-warning frame, preserving divine transcendence by making the direct biological intervention a MEDIATED THREAT (the warning materializes through other means rather than as raw divine biological intervention). The cross-narrative consistency within Bereshit demonstrates a broader Saadyan principle: when the Hebrew describes God directly doing something that an anthropomorphic-immanent reading would frame as mechanical intervention, Saadia routes the action through prophetic-warning vocabulary — whether the action is affective (regret) or biological (womb-closing). The same Form III/IV root surfaces in 6:7 ('as I warned them'); Bereshit 20:18 extends the pattern to the womb-restraint event.

blau_dict.sense: Form I + بـ: 'to prophesy doom / לנבא דבר' (citing Saadia's translations and the Geonim); Form IV + بـ: 'to promise / threaten / decree' (وعد ٢ل٦١ بها = ניבא דבר; the prophetic doom-pronouncement and the announcement of an evil are explicitly merged). Blau's entry directly supports the warning/decreeing-doom sense Saadia uses here. The R2 cross-narrative scan confirms the warning-frame application across both the affective (Gen 6:6-7 וַיִּנָּחֶם) and the direct-biological-intervention (Gen 20:18 עָצַר ה') anti-anthropomorphic categories within Bereshit.

entries.classical_en: boxwood (Buxus sempervirens), a dense slow-growing hardwood; Arabic loanword, ultimately from Persian شمشاد
entries.classical_he: עץ אשכרוע (Buxus sempervirens), עץ קשה וצפוף; שאילה מפרסית שמשאד
entries.saadia_en: boxwood — Saadia identifies the hapax legomenon גֹּפֶר (the wood of Noah's ark) with shamshār (boxwood), a dense durable hardwood prized in the medieval Near East for ship-grade joinery and inlay
entries.saadia_he: עץ אשכרוע — סעדיה מזהה את ה־hapax legomenon "גֹּפֶר" (עץ התיבה) עם שמשאר (אשכרוע), עץ קשה ועמיד שהיה מבוקש במזרח התיכון לעבודות ספנות מדויקות
entries.mechanism: lexical identification: the Hebrew גֹּפֶר occurs only here in the Bible. Saadia substitutes a known, contemporary wood — shamshār — that fits the engineering brief (dense enough not to rot, common enough to be plausible) rather than transliterating an unknown

blau_dict.sense: شمشار (alt شمشاد) "ash-tree / boxwood (Buxus sempervirens) / אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ" — Blau cites Saadia on Gen 6:14 directly (with Ibn Janāḥ's commentary corroborating: "עצי גפר → אלשמשאר"), confirming the medieval Near-Eastern hardwood identification.

entries.classical_en: abyss, vast quantity of water (noun); from the same root as غامرة ("covering, overwhelming") in Gen 1:2
entries.classical_he: תהום, שפע מים עצום (שם עצם); מאותו שורש כמו غامرة ("מציפה") בה ב
entries.saadia_en: the great deeps — Saadia renders the unique phrase מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה ("the fountains of the great deep") as עיון אלג'מר אלעצ'אם ("the springs of the great abysses"), tying the flood narrative back to the primordial water-chaos of Gen 1:2 via the same root غمر
entries.saadia_he: התהומות הגדולות — סעדיה מתרגם את הצירוף הייחודי "מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה" כ"עיון אלג'מר אלעצ'אם" ("מעיינות התהומות הגדולים"), ומקשר בכך את סיפור המבול אל מי התוהו הראשוניים בה ב — באותו השורש غمر
entries.mechanism: Lexical-cosmological linkage, now confirmed as a programmatic 3-BOOK invariance for Heb תְהוֹם → Ar غمر across the entire Pentateuchal cosmological-abyss vocabulary. The noun-form غمر ('abyss, deep') is the mirror-image of the participle غامرة ('covering') that Saadia uses for Heb תֹהוּ at Gen 1:2 (see the related גאמרה TWIST); the systematic cross-attestation across 6 verses in 3 books demonstrates that Saadia treats غمر as the invariant Arabic terminus-technicus for the biblical cosmological-abyss, regardless of register (cosmogonic / flood / song-of-deliverance / patriarchal-blessing): (1) Gen 7:11 — the original flood-anchor: 'נִבְקְעוּ כָּל-מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה' → 'ובקעת גמיע עיון אלג'מר אלעצ'ים' (the abyss-fountains burst open — flood as PARTIAL REVERSION of creation, the abyssal waters Saadia placed beneath the firmament at Gen 1:2 now bursting back up); (2) Gen 8:2 — the flood-closure pillar: 'וַיִּסָּכְרוּ מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם' = 'ואנסדת עיון אלג'מר' (the same fountains now stopped up, the cosmological order restored); (3) Gen 49:25 — Jacob's blessing of Joseph: 'בִּרְכֹת תְּהוֹם רֹבֶצֶת תָּחַת' = 'ברכאת אלג'מר אלראבצה ספלא' ('blessings of the deep crouching below' — the patriarchal-blessing register imports the cosmo-logical-abyss vocabulary as a SOURCE OF FERTILITY); (4) Ex 15:5 — Song of the Sea: 'תְּהֹמֹת יְכַסְיֻמוּ' = 'אלג'מר ג'טאהם' ('the deep covered them' — the Egyptians' destruction as RETURN OF THE ABYSS, mirror of the cosmogonic separation now reversed for the enemy); (5) Ex 15:8 — Song of the Sea continuation: 'קָפְאוּ תְהֹמֹת בְּלֶב-יָם' = 'וגמדת אלג'מר פי קלב אלבחר' ('and the deep was frozen in the heart of the sea' — the abyssal-waters' MIRACULOUS SUSPENSION as inverse-creation, a momentary cosmological stopping-of-time); (6) Deut 33:13 — Moses's blessing of Joseph (the paired-blessing complement to Gen 49:25): 'מִתְּהוֹם רֹבֶצֶת תָּחַת' = 'מן אלג'מר אלג'איצ'ה אלספלא' ('from the deep, sunken, lower' — the patriarchal-blessing register's terminus, framed by the Moses-rewrites-Jacob symmetry). The 3-book cross-Pentateuchal invariance demonstrates Saadia's most consistent cosmological-vocabulary commitment: every biblical تهوم is routed through غمر — whether the context is cosmogonic, deluvial, deliverance-song, or patriarchal-blessing, and whether the abyssal-waters are framed as primordial-chaos, divine-judgment, source-of-blessing, or instrument-of-rescue. Blau attests غمر (אגמאר) as the standard JA noun for 'abyss.' Pedagogically distinctive because the entry now demonstrates the cosmological-vocabulary's systemic reach across the Pentateuch's full thematic register, making this one of the broadest cross-book lexical commitments in the corpus.

blau_dict.sense: Blau (Dict. of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts, s.v. غمر) attests غمر as the standard JA noun for 'abyss / תהום,' citing Saadia's Tafsir at Bereshit 1:2 (אגמאר), Gen 7:11 (the flood-fountains), Ex 15:5/8 (the Song-of-the-Sea deeps), and Deut 33:13 (the Moses-blessing parallel to Gen 49:25). The R2 cross-Pentateuchal scan confirms the systematic invariance across all 6 attestations spanning Bereshit (3 verses: creation-residue at 1:2 plus flood-open/close at 7:11, 8:2, plus patriarchal-blessing at 49:25) + Shemot (2 verses: Song-of-Sea at 15:5, 15:8) + Devarim (1 verse: Moses-blesses-Joseph at 33:13), making غمر the invariant Arabic terminus-technicus for biblical תהום across all 5 Pentateuchal-register contexts.

entries.classical_en: to veil, to screen off, to bar entry (active form I); in the kalam, the technical term for the doctrine of God's being "veiled" from sight
entries.classical_he: להסתיר, להציב מחיצה, למנוע כניסה (בנין I); במונחי הכלאם — מונח טכני לדוקטרינה של היות ה' "מוסתר" מן הראייה
entries.saadia_en: screened him off — Saadia renders the strikingly intimate וַיִּסְגֹּר יְהוָה בַּעֲדוֹ ("and the LORD shut [the door] behind him") as וחגב אללה דונה ("and God screened him off"), avoiding any image of God personally closing Noah inside the ark
entries.saadia_he: החריג אותו, חצץ בעדו — סעדיה מתרגם את הפסוק האינטימי במיוחד "וַיִּסְגֹּר יְהוָה בַּעֲדוֹ" כ"וחגב אללה דונה" ("וְחָצַץ אלוהים בעדו"), ומונע כל תמונה של ה' הסוגר אישית את הדלת על נוח
entries.mechanism: Anti-anthropomorphic divine-concealment vocabulary, now confirmed across 2 books with the Devarim divine-face-hiding extension. Saadia uses Ar حجب ('to veil, to screen, to conceal' — the kalām technical term for God's being veiled from creaturely vision) as his invariant anti-anthropomorphic verb for biblical divine-action that would otherwise imply a physical-spatial concealment-gesture. The cross-book arc: (1) Bereshit 7:16 — the ark-sealing pillar: 'וַיִּסְגֹּר ה' בַּעֲדוֹ' = 'וחגב אללה בעאדה' ('and YHWH SCREENED behind him'). The Heb סָגַר ('shut/closed') implies a physical hand on the ark's door; Saadia routes this through the generic screening-action حجب, depersonalizing the divine gesture. (2) Devarim 31:18 — the divine-face-hiding pillar: 'וְאָנֹכִי הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר פָּנַי בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא' = 'אנא מקים עלי' חגב רחמתי ענהם פי ד'אלך אלזמאן' ('I am persisting in SCREENING my mercy from them at that time'). Saadia routes BOTH the verb (סָתַר 'hide' → حجب 'screen/veil') AND the object (פָּנַי 'my face' → רחמתי 'my mercy') through anti-anthropomorphic transformations: the Heb divine-face anthropomorphism is replaced with the abstract divine-mercy attribute, and the physical hiding-of-face is replaced with the philosophical screening-of-divine-presence. The Devarim 31:18 attestation thus EXTENDS the مكانيكي 'shut behind' Gen 7:16 case to the more strongly anthropomorphic 'hide-my-face' divine-absence case — both routed through the same screening-vocabulary حجب, with the kalām resonance pulling the verb into Saadia's broader theological discourse of divine-transcendence. The verb's philosophical weight (kalām: God 'veiled' from creaturely vision; the standard medieval term for the divine ḥijāb separating Creator from creation) makes حجب a load-bearing entry in Saadia's anti-anthropo-morphic vocabulary, used not as a one-off substitution but as a programmatic translational anchor for ALL biblical concealment-of-divine-presence verbs across the Pentateuch. Pedagogically distinctive because the cross-book extension surfaces the entry's broader scope: Saadia uses حجب for biblical divine-action involving ANY concealment-frame (sealing-of-ark + hiding-of-face), preserving divine transcendence through a single Arabic philosophical-screening verb.

blau_dict.sense: حجب 'to veil, to screen, to conceal' — Blau attests the kalām-technical sense of حجب as the standard medieval term for the divine ḥijāb separating Creator from creation, citing Saadia's Tafsir on Gen 7:16 (וַיִּסְגֹּר → וחגב) and Saadia's own Emunot ve-Deot for the philosophical extension. The R2 cross-book scan confirms the Devarim 31:18 attestation (הסתר אסתיר → חגב), demonstrating that Saadia deploys the same screening-vocabulary across both the ark-sealing (Gen 7:16) and the divine-face-hiding (Deut 31:18) anti-anthropomorphic categories, making حجب a 2-book program for biblical concealment-of-divine-presence.

entries.classical_en: Mount Qardū / Cudi (Jabal Jūdī in classical Arabic geography) — the mountain range in southeastern Anatolia / northern Iraq traditionally identified as the landing-place of Noah's ark in Targumic, Syriac, and Islamic sources
entries.classical_he: הר קרדו / ג'ודי (ג'בל ג'ודי בגיאוגרפיה ערבית קלאסית) — רכס הרים בדרום-מזרח אנטוליה / צפון עיראק, שזוהה במסורת הארמית, הסורית והאסלאמית כמקום עגינת תיבת נוח
entries.saadia_en: Mount Qardū — Saadia renders the Hebrew הָרֵי אֲרָרָט ("mountains of Ararat") as גבאל קרדא, naming the specific peak rather than the broader Urartu region; this aligns Saadia with the Targumic identification (Targum Onqelos: טוּרֵי קַרְדּוּ) and the Qur'anic Jūdī (Q 11:44) against the Armenian-highlands rendering
entries.saadia_he: הרי קרדו — סעדיה מתרגם "הָרֵי אֲרָרָט" העברי כ"גבאל קרדא", ומנכס פסגה ספציפית במקום אזור אררט הרחב; זיהוי זה תואם את האונקלוסי ("טוּרֵי קַרְדּוּ") ואת הג'ודי הקוראני (סורה יא, מד), בניגוד לתרגום של רמת ארמניה
entries.mechanism: geographical identification by tradition: Saadia harmonizes with the Aramaic-Targumic and Islamic-geographical consensus on the ark's landing-place — Mt. Cudi in upper Mesopotamia, not the Armenian Ararat peak

entries.classical_en: offering, sacrifice (well-attested classical Arabic, with Qur'anic usage — Q 3:183, Q 5:27 — for sacrificial offerings)
entries.classical_he: קרבן, מנחה (מילה ערבית קלאסית מוכרת; שכיחה גם בקוראן — סורה ג קפג, ה כז — בהקשר של הקרבת קרבנות)
entries.saadia_en: the pleasing offering — Saadia renders the densely anthropomorphic וַיָּרַח יְהוָה אֶת-רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ ("and the LORD smelled the soothing aroma") as פקבל אללה אלקרבאן אלמרצ'י ("and God accepted the pleasing offering"), substituting acceptance for olfaction and a noun ("the offering") for the sensory predicate ("the aroma")
entries.saadia_he: הקרבן הרצוי — סעדיה מתרגם את הפסוק האנתרופומורפי במיוחד "וַיָּרַח יְהוָה אֶת-רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ" כ"פקבל אללה אלקרבאן אלמרצ'י" ("וקיבל ה' את הקרבן הרצוי"), ומחליף את הרחת הריח בקבלה של הקרבן עצמו
entries.mechanism: anti-anthropomorphic double-substitution: (1) the verb is shifted from יָּרַח ("smelled") to قَبِلَ ("accepted") — God does not have a nose; (2) the object is shifted from רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ ("the soothing aroma") to אלקרבאן אלמרצ'י ("the pleasing offering") — Saadia gives a thing for God to receive (the sacrifice) rather than a sensory quality God would have to perceive

entries.classical_en: Form IV of ورد — "to cause [something] to come forth, to send / dispatch"; form I ورد in classical usage means "to descend (to a watering place), to arrive at"
entries.classical_he: בנין IV של ו-ר-ד — "להוציא, לשלוח, להפנות [דבר־מה]"; בנין I ורד בלשון הקלאסית: "לרדת [אל מקור מים], להגיע אל"
entries.saadia_en: brought forth — Saadia's stock substitution for the anthropomorphic וַיֵּרֶד יְהוָה ("and the LORD descended") at Babel: פאורד אללה אמרא מוגהא ("and God brought forth a directed command"). The divine descent is replaced by the dispatch of an executive command. The same idiom appears in verse 7 ("let us go down, let us confound their language" → "let us bring forth a directed command, that we may scatter their languages")
entries.saadia_he: הוציא, שלח — תרגומו הקבוע של סעדיה למילה האנתרופומורפית "וַיֵּרֶד יְהוָה" במגדל בבל: "פאורד אללה אמרא מוגהא" ("וְהוציא ה' אֲמירה מכוונת"). הירידה האלוהית מוחלפת בשליחת פקודה ביצועית. אותו הצירוף חוזר גם בפסוק ז ("הָבָה נֵרְדָה וְנָבְלָה" → "הבה נוציא אֲמירה מכוונת, ובה נפזר את לשונותיהם")
entries.mechanism: Anti-anthropomorphic dispatch-frame — paradigmatic Saadia substitution for biblical divine-descent narratives where YHWH is described as physically 'coming down' (יָרַד) to investigate-and-act in human space. God does not descend; God dispatches an 'amr muwajjah' — a 'directed command,' Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic euphemism for mediated divine intervention. The dispatch-frame applies INVARIANTLY across the two Bereshit YHWH-comes-down-to-investigate anchors: (1) Babel at Gen 11:5, 11:7 (the original anchors — וַיֵּרֶד ה' לִרְאֹת → אורד אמרא מוגהא ליתאמל: 'I dispatch a directed command and observe'); (2) Sodom at Gen 18:21 (אֵרֲדָה-נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה → אורד אמרא מוגהא ואנצר: same Form-IV dispatch-verb + same idiom 'directed command' + same observation-frame). The cross-narrative consistency within Bereshit confirms Saadia's programmatic management of divine-descent-to-investigate verses: wherever the Hebrew has YHWH coming down to observe-and-act in human space (Babel + Sodom), Saadia routes the move through the impersonal 'directed command' dispatched from above, preserving divine transcendence. EMPIRICAL SCOPE-CORRECTION (Phase 3 R2 Batch 2): the previous mechanism prose claimed the dispatch-frame applied to 'Sodom, Sinai, the Tent of Meeting' — but the R2 B2 cross-book scan demonstrates that this overreached. At the Sinai-descent verses (Ex 19:11, 19:18, 19:20, 34:5) and the Tent-of-Meeting-descent verses (Num 11:25, 12:5), Saadia consistently uses Form V تجلَّى ('manifest in cloud/fire') — a SEPARATE anti-anthropomorphic strategy that routes the divine-descent through a manifestation-frame rather than a dispatch-frame. The two strategies are structurally distinct: the dispatch-frame (ورد) is used where the Heb has YHWH descending to INVESTIGATE human action (Babel + Sodom); the manifestation-frame (تجلَّى) is used where the Heb has YHWH descending to MANIFEST presence-and-speech in cultic space (Sinai theophany + Tent of Meeting). The dispatch-frame is bounded to 3 Bereshit verses (11:5, 11:7, 18:21). The تجلَّى manifestation cluster is logged as a candidate for a separate future TWIST entry (Phase 3 R3) — see PHASE3_R2_BATCH2_SESSION_NOTES.md for the empirical finding. Blau notes that ورد itself is Saadia's standard calque for Hebrew יר״ד in his Bible translations; the Form-IV causative (the form actually used here) is the causative of this calqued descent-sense — 'to cause to come down,' i.e., to dispatch.

blau_dict.sense: Form I: 'to descend / הוריד' — Blau explicitly labels this a 'תרגום שאילה (loan-translation) from יר״ד in Bible translations,' citing Saadia's Tafsir on Tehillim 28:1 and 49:18 and noting that the calque is widespread in his renderings of Bible passages. Form IV (the form actually used here) is the causative of this calqued descent-sense — 'to cause to come down,' i.e., to dispatch. The R2 Batch 2 empirical scope-correction bounds the dispatch-frame to the Bereshit YHWH-comes-down-to-INVESTIGATE pillars (Babel at Gen 11:5, 11:7 + Sodom at Gen 18:21); the Sinai (Ex 19:11, 19:18, 19:20, 34:5) and Tent-of-Meeting (Num 11:25, 12:5) descent verses use Form V تجلَّى manifestation-vocabulary, a structurally distinct anti-anthropomorphic strategy. The two strategies cluster the dispatch-frame to investigation-contexts and the manifestation-frame to cultic-theophany contexts.

entries.classical_en: kiln, furnace (esp. a lime-kiln or potter's furnace); Arabic loanword from the Aramaic אַתּוּן, used in Daniel 3 for Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace
entries.classical_he: כבשן, אש (בפרט כבשן סיד או יוצרים); שאילה ערבית מן הארמית אַתּוּן, ובלשון הזאת בדניאל ג לכבשן נבוכדנאצר
entries.saadia_en: the furnace of the Chaldeans — Saadia renders אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים ("Ur of the Chaldees," Abraham's hometown) as אתון אלכסדאניין ("the furnace of the Chaldeans"), reading the Hebrew אוּר not as the proper name of a Mesopotamian city but as "fire / kiln" — adopting the well-known rabbinic Aggadah of Abraham being cast into Nimrod's furnace
entries.saadia_he: כבשן הכשדים — סעדיה מתרגם את "אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים" ("אור כשדים", עיר הולדתו של אברהם) כ"אתון אלכסדאניין" ("כבשן הכשדים"), וקורא את "אור" העברי לא כשם עצם של עיר מסופוטמית, אלא כ"אש / כבשן" — בנוסח האגדה הידועה על השלכת אברהם לכבשן של נמרוד
entries.mechanism: Midrashic identification / lexical re-reading, now confirmed across the full Bereshit Abraham-narrative cluster (3 verses, all Bereshit, anchored on the same Ur-as-furnace midrashic commitment). Saadia commits to the Bereshit Rabbah 38:13 + Pirqei De-Rabbi Eliezer 26 tradition that Haran died in Nimrod's furnace and Abraham was tested there; the Aramaic loanword אַתּוּן (from Daniel 3, where it names the Babylonian fiery-furnace into which the three companions are cast) is deployed as a SYSTEMATIC bridge between biblical Heb אוּר ('Ur', the toponym) and the Aggadic furnace-tradition. The cross-pericope consistency across the three Patriarchal Abraham-genealogy verses: (1) Gen 11:28 — Haran dies 'in Ur of the Chaldees' = 'באתון אלכסדאניין' (the Aggadic-furnace; the midrashic claim is that Haran was burned in Nimrod's trial-furnace before Abraham was rescued); (2) Gen 11:31 — Terah's family migration: 'they went out from Ur of the Chaldees' = 'כ'רגו מן אתון אלכסדאניין' (they went out from the FURNACE — the toponymic-Ur is fully absorbed into the midrashic-furnace identification); (3) Gen 15:7 — the divine self-introduction at the Covenant-Between-the-Pieces: 'אֲנִי ה' אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים' = 'אנא אללה אלד'י אכ'רגתך מן אתון אלכסדאניין' ('I am the deity who brought you out from the FURNACE of the Chaldees'). The Gen 15:7 attestation is structurally significant: it is the DIVINE-SPEECH-ACT confirmation of the midrashic-furnace claim — God himself names the rescue as 'bringing-out-from-the-furnace,' aligning the foundational covenant-narrative with the Aggadic-furnace tradition. The cross-pericope consistency confirms that Saadia operates with a fixed midrashic-lexical commitment: every Pentateuchal mention of אוּר כַּשְׂדִים is routed through the Aramaic-loan furnace-vocabulary, never as a toponymic-Ur. The choice is structurally midrashic: the Aramaic-loan אַתּוּן (from Daniel 3:6 ff) is the linguistic pivot that connects the Patriarchal-narrative to the Babylonian-exile fiery-furnace tradition, making Abraham's rescue typologically parallel to the three companions' rescue. Pedagogically distinctive because the entry demonstrates Saadia's willingness to commit to a controversial Aggadic-tradition AT THE LEXICAL LEVEL — not just as commentary but as fixed translational choice — across the full Abraham-foundational-narrative arc. (Note: blau_dict remains None — this is one of the saadia-direct-only entries explicitly noted in PHASE3_R1's no-cite-audit; Blau has no entry for the Aramaic-loan אַתּוּן in the JA fiery-furnace sense.)

entries.classical_en: judge; ruler; arbitrator — one who decides between disputants. Active participle of حكم "to judge, to govern."
entries.classical_he: שופט, מושל, פוסק — צורת הבינוני הפועל של חכ"ם ("לשפוט", "לפסוק")
entries.saadia_en: decreeing — Saadia inserts the circumstantial accusative חאכמא ("as one who decrees") into divine-speech verses where the Hebrew has לאמר, recasting God's "saying" as a binding juridical decree rather than a mere utterance. Beyond the inserted use, Saadia keeps the ordinary judicial sense ("a judge") in legal narrative.
entries.saadia_he: פוסק, גוזר — סעדיה מוסיף את חאכמא ("בתורת גוזר") כצורת חוגית בפסוקי דיבור אלוהי המסתיימים בלאמר, וממיר את ה"דיבור" האלוהי בגזרת-דין מחייבת ולא באמירה גרידא. כאשר ההקשר משפטי (לא דיבור אלוהי), שומר סעדיה על המשמע הקלסי של "שופט"
entries.mechanism: Anti-anthropomorphic interpretive insertion, now confirmed across THREE books in the divine-speech register. Saadia inserts the circumstantial-accusative participle حاكمًا ('as a decreer / acting-as-judge') into divine speech-acts to avoid portraying God as 'speaking' directly. The construction routes the Heb's bare לאמר / וָאֹמַר ('saying' / 'and I said') through an indirect frame: God doesn't speak — God judicially-decrees, with حاكمًا naming the modality of the divine speech-act. Standard Saadianic move documented in saadia-gloss-table.json; built on the well-attested judicial sense of حكم. The cross-Pentateuchal arc now spans (1) the divine-blessing speech-act in Bereshit 1:22 (וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים לֵאמֹר → ובארכהם אללה חאכמא — the FIRST recorded divine speech-act in scripture, marked from the outset with the non-anthropomorphic frame); (2) the Mosaic-judicial speech-acts in Shemot 2:14 (וַיֹּאמֶר מִי שָׂמְךָ לְאִישׁ שַׂר וְשֹׁפֵט עָלֵינוּ → אלחאכם — Moses confronted as 'the decreer/judge') and 22:27 (אֱלֹהִים לֹא תְקַלֵּל וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ → לא תהון בחאכם — the elohim-as-judges passage); AND (3) the Vayikra divine-promise speech-act at 20:24 (וָאֹמַר לָכֶם אַתֶּם תִּירְשׁוּ אֶת אַדְמָתָם → וקלת לכם חאכמא — 'I said to you, AS DECREER, you shall possess their land'). The Vayikra 20:24 attestation is structurally significant: it is the FIRST divine-promise speech-act in the Levitical land-vocabulary register, and Saadia routes it through exactly the same non-anthropomorphic insertion as the Bereshit 1:22 creation-blessing. The cross-book consistency confirms that the circumstantial-accusative חאכמא is not a one-off Bereshit-1 anti-anthropomorphic move but Saadia's programmatic strategy for the divine speech-act category across the Pentateuch — wherever YHWH 'says' something covenantally-binding, the insertion names the modality as judicial-decree rather than vocal-utterance. Distinct from the bare-form judicial חאכם / אלחאכם used for human judges in Ex 21:6, 22:7-8 and Deut 17:9ff (different register: judicial-administrative, not divine-speech-modifier; see Phase 4 Devarim B1 session notes line 158-160). Pedagogically distinctive because the entry now demonstrates Saadia's systematic management of divine speech-acts across all three major covenantal speech-modes (blessing, judgment-context, promise-of-land), spanning Bereshit + Shemot + Vayikra.

blau_dict.sense: Blau (Dict. of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts, s.v. חכם) attests Form III 'to judge / שפט, דן' alongside Forms I/II/V — the judicial sense Saadia builds on when inserting the participle حاكمًا at לאמר / וָאֹמַר. Blau does not name the inserted-participle pattern itself; the divergence here is in Saadia's syntactic deployment of an otherwise-classical sense. The R2 cross-book scan confirms the systematic invariance across three covenantal divine-speech-act registers — creation-blessing (Gen 1:22), Mosaic-judicial framing (Ex 2:14, 22:27), and Levitical land-promise (Lev 20:24) — and excludes the judicial-administrative חאכם cluster (Ex 21-22, Deut 17ff) as a distinct register from the divine-speech-act insertion.

entries.classical_en: jewel, gem, precious stone; (philosophical, post-classical) substance, essence — the underlying material of which something consists
entries.classical_he: אבן יקרה, אבן חן; (בפילוסופיה) עצם, מהות — החומר היסודי שממנו דבר עשוי
entries.saadia_en: [precious] substance — Saadia renders the Tablets of the Covenant as לוחי אלגוהר ("the Tablets of substance"). The choice reflects the midrashic identification (b. Nedarim 38a, Tanḥuma) that the Tablets were hewn from a precious-stone material (sapphire, סנפירין). جوهر carries both the concrete "jewel" sense and the philosophical "substance" sense — Saadia exploits both at once
entries.saadia_he: עצם, חומר יקר — סעדיה מתרגם את "לוחות הברית" כ"לוחי אלגוהר" (לוחות הגוהר). הבחירה משקפת את המסורת המדרשית (נדרים לח ע"א, תנחומא) שלפיה לוחות הברית נחצבו מאבן יקרה (סַנפירין). جوهر בעצמו נושא בעת ובעונה אחת את המשמע הקונקרטי ("אבן יקרה") ואת המשמע הפילוסופי ("עצם, מהות")
entries.mechanism: Midrashic identification + philosophical vocabulary — now confirmed across the FULL Pentateuchal Tablets-tradition arc (Shemot + Devarim, 9 verses). Saadia uses a single Arabic term جوهر that operates on two registers — JEWEL (the rabbinic tradition of Tablets-of-sapphire, b. Sotah 17a; Tanḥuma Ki Tissa 26) and SUBSTANCE/ESSENCE (the philosophical claim of Tablets-of-divine-essence, drawing on the kalām/falsafa technical sense of jawhar as 'substance' or 'essential being'). The dual-register move renders Heb לֻחֹת so the reader hears BOTH the rabbinic tradition and the philosophical claim simultaneously. The cross-book arc now spans (1) the Sinai Tablets-promise at Ex 24:12 ('אֶת-לֻחֹת הָאֶבֶן' → 'לוחי אלגוהר' — the FIRST mention of the Tablets in scripture, marked from the outset with the dual-register vocabulary); (2) the giving-of-Tablets pillar at Ex 31:18 ('לֻחֹת אֶבֶן כְּתֻבִים בְּאֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים' = 'לוחי גוהר מכתובין בקדרה' אללה' — the divine-finger written register, with the anthropomorphic 'finger' simultaneously routed through Saadia's standard בקדרה' anti-anthropomorphic 'by-power-of' substitution); (3) the second-Tablets re-issue at Ex 34:1 ('פְּסָל-לְךָ שְׁנֵי-לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים' = 'אנחת לוחי גוהר'); (4) Moses descending Sinai with the second Tablets at Ex 34:4 ('וַיִּקַּח בְּיָדוֹ שְׁנֵי לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים' = 'ואכ'ד' מעה לוחי אלגוהר'); AND the Devarim retrospective cluster (Deut 5:19, 9:9, 9:10, 10:1, 10:3 — Moses's reflective recount of the Tablets-events). The cross-Pentateuchal consistency demonstrates that the dual-register Tablets-vocabulary is Saadia's INVARIANT lexical signature for the Tablets across both the narrative (Shemot) and the homiletic (Devarim) registers — never deviating into a single-register sense, even when the surrounding context might invite it. Pedagogically distinctive because the entry now demonstrates that Saadia treats the Tablets-as-jewel-and-essence as a fixed terminus-technicus across the entire Sinai-vocabulary system. Distinct from the breastplate-jeweler usage at Ex 28:11, 28:17, 31:5, 35:33, 39:10, where Saadia uses جوهر for Heb אֶבֶן in the bare classical jewel-sense (one register only — the literal jeweler's-craft register, not the dual Tablets-register move) — see the deferred bucket for those cases.

blau_dict.sense: Blau (Dict. of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts, s.v. גוהר / جوهر) cites the dual-register sense — both 'jewel/precious stone' (the rabbinic-poetic register) and 'substance/essence' (the falsafa technical sense, Saadia's own Emunot ve-Deot uses the same term for the philosophical substance-category). The R2 cross-book scan confirms Saadia deploys this dual-register Arabic term invariantly for biblical לֻחֹת across BOTH the Shemot Sinai-narrative attestations (Ex 24:12, 31:18, 34:1, 34:4) AND the Devarim retrospective attestations (Deut 5:19, 9:9, 9:10, 10:1, 10:3), making the Tablets-vocabulary a 2-book program with 9 verse attestations.

entries.classical_en: Form I (دلج dalaja): to travel by night, set out before dawn. Form IV (أدلج adlaja): to travel late at night, just before daybreak. The classical sense centers on the night-journey, not the dawn-rising itself
entries.classical_he: בנין I (دلج): ללכת בלילה, לצאת לדרך לפני שחר. בנין IV (أدلج): לנסוע בלילה לקראת השחר. המשמע הקלסי מתמקד בנסיעה הלילית עצמה, לא בקימה המוקדמת
entries.saadia_en: rose early in the morning — Saadia uses أدلج as the standard Arabic equivalent of Hebrew הִשְׁכִּים ("rose early at dawn"), regardless of whether any night-travel is involved. The participle / perfective covers the simple "early rising" of biblical heroes (Abraham at the Akedah, the spies, Moses on Sinai)
entries.saadia_he: השכים — סעדיה מתרגם בקביעות את הפועל העברי "השכים" באמצעות أدلج (אדלג), גם כאשר אין מדובר בנסיעה לילית כלל אלא בקימה מוקדמת בבוקר
entries.mechanism: Post-classical semantic shift, now confirmed across the entire Pentateuchal 'rise-early' narrative tradition — 13 verses across THREE books. Saadia uses أَدْلَجَ (Form IV of دلج, classical 'to travel by night, to set out before dawn') as the invariant equivalent of Heb הִשְׁכִּים (Hiphil of שכם, 'to rise early in the morning' — the canonical biblical Patriarchal-and-Mosaic narrative formula for purposive early-morning departure). Classical Arabic narrows أدلج specifically to NIGHT-travel; Saadia exploits the post-classical broadening (already attested in Lisān al-ʿArab) to a generic 'early-morning departure' frame, then deploys it as the systematic Pentateuchal terminus-technicus. The cross-book attestation arc spans: (1) the full Bereshit Patriarchal sequence — Abraham at Abimelech's court (20:8) → Abraham casting out Hagar (21:14) → AKEDAH (22:3 — the canonical 'rose early' verse of the binding) → Isaac–Abimelech treaty (26:31) → Jacob at Bethel after the dream (28:18) → Laban after the Mizpah covenant (32:1) → Abraham overlooking Sodom (19:27, the original anchor); (2) the Shemot Mosaic plague-and-covenant sequence — Moses at the Nile before Pharaoh (8:16) → Moses for the hail-plague announcement (9:13) → Moses building the Sinai-covenant altar (24:4) → the golden-calf morning offerings (32:6) → Moses ascending Sinai with the second tablets (34:4); (3) the Bamidbar ma'apilim attempt at the Mt. Hor breach (14:40, the original cross-book anchor). Across all 13 attestations Heb הִשְׁכִּים/וַיַּשְׁכֵּם is rendered with the same Form IV أدلج + variants (פאדלג / ואדלג / ואדלגו / פאדלגו), with the standard adverbial-phrase באלג'דאה ('at-the-dawn') almost always trailing — a fixed Saadyan idiom for the Heb בַּבֹּקֶר. The cross-Pentateuchal-arc invariance is the strongest evidence in the corpus that Saadia operates with stable narrative-formula vocabulary: every 'rose-early' Patriarchal or Mosaic departure receives the same Arabic lexical signature, regardless of speaker (Abraham, Hagar, Isaac, Jacob, Laban, Moses, the Israelites) or context (private journey, treaty-ratification, cultic encounter, military departure). Pedagogically distinctive because the verse-count (13) and the cross-book breadth (3 books spanning Patriarchal → Mosaic → Wilderness) make this the single largest narrative-formula promotion in the corpus.

blau_dict.sense: Blau (Dict. of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts, s.v. דלג) explicitly cites Saadia's Tafsir on Exodus 8:16 — 'השכם בבקר' rendered as 'אדלג באלגדאה' — as the canonical example of the post-classical semantic transition from 'to travel by night' → 'to rise early.' Blau notes that the same shift is already attested in classical Arabic Lisān al-ʿArab, and that Saadia adopts it as his standard equivalent of הִשְׁכִּים. The R2 cross-book scan confirms the systematic invariance across 13 attestations spanning Bereshit (7 verses) + Shemot (5 verses) + Bamidbar (1 verse), making אדלג the broadest narrative-formula calque in the divergence corpus.

entries.classical_en: Form V تجسّس, the idiomatic Arabic verb for tactile groping
entries.classical_he: תְּגַסַּס בבניין החמישי, הוא הפועל הערבי הרגיל לְמִשּׁוּשׁ
entries.saadia_en: Form II جسّس, mirroring Hebrew Pi'el גישש
entries.saadia_he: ג'סס בבניין השני, מקבילה מורפולוגית לפיעל העברי גישש
entries.mechanism: Saadia chooses Arabic Form II (geminate-doubled root) over the more idiomatic Form V; the choice tracks the Hebrew Pi'el verb גישש morphologically, which Blau reads as the Hebrew form shaping the Arabic morphological selection.

blau_dict.sense: Form II جسّس 'to grope, to feel' — Blau records that bringing the verb from non-Jewish sources weakens any hypothesis of direct Hebrew גישש influence, but the Form II pairing with Hebrew Pi'el is itself the marked feature. Cited on Gen 31:34 and (groping prophecy) Deut 28:29 / Isa 59:10.

entries.classical_en: for your sake, on your account
entries.classical_he: בְּגְלָלֵךְ
entries.saadia_en: on your account
entries.mechanism: JA preposition بـ + جريرة 'on account of'; Saadia renders the Hebrew idiomatic בִּגְלָלֵךְ with a non-cognate Arabic phrasing Blau treats as standard medieval JA usage.

blau_dict.sense: بجريرة 'because of, on account of' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 12:13 directly (compare من جريرة in the same construction).

entries.classical_en: sheaves of grain, bundles bound after reaping
entries.classical_he: אֲלֻמִּים
entries.saadia_en: sheaves
entries.mechanism: Non-cognate dialectal pairing: Saadia uses Arabic root ج-ر-ز for Hebrew אלומה rather than the better-known Arabic حزمة; Blau treats the lemma جزّزة under root جرز.

blau_dict.sense: جزّزة (related to جرز) 'sheaf, bundle' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 37:7 ('מאלמים אלימים' = נגרז גרזא); compare Saadia on Ps 126:6 'נושא אלמתיו' = ויחמל גרזה.

entries.classical_en: as espionage, on a spying-mission
entries.classical_he: כִּמְרַגְּלִים
entries.saadia_en: as espionage
entries.mechanism: Saadia recasts the Hebrew predicate-noun idiom כִּמְרַגְּלִים ('as spies') with an Arabic abstract verbal-noun construction بـ + جساسة ('in espionage'). The lemma is a regularly-formed Form-I action noun.

blau_dict.sense: جساسة 'espionage' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 42:30 directly ('כי אתנו כמרגלים את הארץ' = ואתהמונא בגסאסה אלבלד).

entries.classical_en: firstborn-right, primogeniture status
entries.classical_he: בְּכֹרָה
entries.saadia_en: birthright
entries.mechanism: Standard JA noun for the legal status; Blau treats it under primogeniture rather than as a general 'firstness' abstract.

blau_dict.sense: بكورية 'primogeniture' (alongside 'virginity'); Blau attests in the inheritance sense citing Saadia on Gen 25:31-34, noting alternation with the variant بكورة.

entries.classical_en: those of the third (generation), great-grandchildren
entries.classical_he: בְּנֵי שִׁלֵּשִׁים
entries.saadia_en: (children) of the third generation
entries.mechanism: Saadia uses Arabic plural ثوالث (lit. 'thirds') as a fixed substantival for the biblical-Hebrew kinship term שלשים; Blau treats it as a denominative that surfaces also at Ex 20:5 (شَلاشِيم).

blau_dict.sense: ثوالث (plural of ثالث) 'those of the third generation' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 50:23 ('בני שלשים' = ת'ואלת'א) and the parallel at Ex 20:5.

entries.classical_en: grace, favor
entries.classical_he: חֵן
entries.saadia_en: favor
entries.mechanism: Saadia uses Arabic حظاء — formally a plural of حظوة 'favor', but here used as a singular — for Hebrew חֵן ('favor in the eyes of').

blau_dict.sense: حظاء 'grace, favor' — ostensibly plural of حظوة but Saadia uses it as a singular; Blau records the JA usage citing Saadia on Gen 39:21.

entries.classical_en: an evil rumor, slander
entries.classical_he: דִּבָּה רָעָה
entries.saadia_en: an evil report
entries.mechanism: Non-cognate substantive: Saadia renders Hebrew דבה רעה ('an evil report') with the Arabic abstract شناعة 'rumor, slander' rather than the cognate دباب-derivatives.

blau_dict.sense: شناعة 'rumor, slander' (not necessarily 'evil rumor') — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 37:2.

entries.classical_en: midsummer heat (the hottest part of summer)
entries.classical_he: קַיִץ
entries.saadia_en: midsummer heat
entries.mechanism: Register choice: Saadia uses قيظ (specifically the hot core of summer) rather than the general صَيْف; the lexical pairing with cognate-sounding Hebrew קַיִץ is precise rather than approximate.

blau_dict.sense: قيظ 'summer (heat)' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 8:22.

entries.classical_en: lion, lioness (high-register synonym)
entries.classical_he: לָבִיא
entries.saadia_en: lion
entries.mechanism: High-register synonym: Saadia preserves the biblical-Hebrew elevation of לָבִיא over the prosaic אַרְיֵה by reaching for لبوة (formally f.) used as a masculine; the Aggron also pairs لبو ~ לביא.

blau_dict.sense: لبو(ة) 'lion (lioness, used m.)' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 49:9 and the Aggron 262:1 (לביא לבו).

entries.classical_en: a kind of small fierce viper
entries.classical_he: שְׁפִיפֹן
entries.saadia_en: a striking viper
entries.mechanism: Non-cognate dialectal pairing: Saadia uses Arabic مطرون (Blau-Festschrift area 143-145) for Hebrew שְׁפִיפֹן — a regional Arabic term for the same viper class, not derivable from the standard ثعبان used elsewhere in the verse for נָחָשׁ.

blau_dict.sense: مطرون 'a kind of viper' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 49:17 ('שפיפון עלי אורח' = וכאלמטרון).

entries.classical_en: Classical Arabic نقل = 'transport, transfer, carrying-from-one-place-to-another'; never the default rendering for biblical 'forced labor' or 'burden' (which would expect عمل, تكليف, or حمل).
entries.classical_he: בערבית הקלאסית نقل = 'הובלה, העברה, נשיאה ממקום למקום'; אינה הברירה הרגילה ל'עבודת פרך' או 'מעמסה' במקרא (שמצופה עבורן عمل, تكليف, או حمل).
entries.saadia_en: the transport-labor (of the Egyptians), the load-carrying burden
entries.mechanism: Semantic-field calque across the Egypt-slavery pericope: Hebrew סֵבֶל ('burden, forced labor') gets a unified Saadian rendering as نقل — narrowing the abstract 'burden' to the concrete 'transport/relocation' of building materials. The choice routes the entire slavery vocabulary through a logistics-frame rather than a labor-pain frame (Heb עָנָה→Ar تعذيب, but Heb סֵבֶל→Ar نقل). Blau notes that Rashbam 11 follows Saadia's reading. The pairing surfaces invariantly across Gen 49:15 (ויט שכמו לסבל = פימד ענקה ללנקל) and the Exodus-slavery cluster (Ex 1:11, 2:11, 5:4, 5:5, 6:6, 6:7), making it Saadia's standing equivalent for סבל in the Genesis-Exodus narrative.

blau_dict.sense: نقل 'transportation of a load, carrying' (used to render Mishnaic-style סבל) — Blau cites Saadia on Gen 49:15 ('ויט שכמו לסבל' = פימד ענקה ללנקל) and the full Exodus-slavery cluster (Ex 1:11, 2:11, 5:4-5, 6:6-7), with Rashbam 11 following the equivalence.

entries.classical_en: Form I سعى, classically 'to strive, walk briskly'
entries.classical_he: סעי בבניין הראשון, פירושו המוקדם הוא 'להתאמץ, ללכת במהירות'
entries.saadia_en: Form I سعى extended semantically to 'teem, swarm, multiply'
entries.saadia_he: סעי בבניין הראשון, מורחב סמנטית ל'רחש, שרץ, התרבה'
entries.mechanism: Saadia stretches Arabic سعى (classically 'to strive, run') to render Hebrew שָׁרַץ ('teem, multiply'). The extension brings the verb into the biblical reproductive-blessing field; Blau treats it as a marked semantic widening rather than a standard equivalence.

blau_dict.sense: سعى 'in all its biblical senses (creep, teem, multiply, be fruitful)' — Blau records the wide extension citing Saadia.

entries.classical_en: to give in marriage, the unmarked verb for 'I gave (her) (to him)' for a daughter-in-law
entries.classical_he: לתת, להעניק (פועל סתמי לתיאור מתן בת לאיש)
entries.saadia_en: Form II زوّج 'to marry off' — sharpens the legal kind of giving
entries.saadia_he: זוג' בבניין השני, 'להשיא, לחתן' — מחדד את אופי המתן המשפטי
entries.mechanism: Saadia reads Hebrew נְתַתִּיהָ ('I gave her') not as a generic transfer but specifically as a marriage transaction, rendering with Form II زوّج 'to marry off' rather than the general أعطى.

blau_dict.sense: زوج Form II '(with و-)' 'to form a marriage alliance, give in marriage' — Blau records the JA usage; here on Gen 38:26 Saadia sharpens the Hebrew נְתַתִּיהָ into a marriage-specific act.

entries.classical_en: (his heart) grew faint, slackened — the physiological reading of וַיָּפָג
entries.classical_he: (לבו) פג, נחלש פיזית — הקריאה הפיזיולוגית של וַיָּפָג
entries.saadia_en: (his heart) doubted — Form II شكّك 'to cause to doubt'
entries.saadia_he: (לבו) הטיל ספק, חשש — שכך בבניין השני 'גרם להטיל ספק'
entries.mechanism: Saadia reframes Jacob's reaction from physical faintness to cognitive doubt: וַיָּפָג לִבּוֹ ('his heart grew faint') becomes פשכך קלבה ('his heart doubted'). The verse's own continuation — 'because he did not believe them' — supports the cognitive reading Saadia pulls forward into the main verb.

blau_dict.sense: Form II شكّك 'to cause doubt'; Blau records the JA Form II citing Saadia on Gen 45:26 ('ויפג לבו' = פשכך קלבה).

entries.classical_en: their weapons — the standard rendering of the disputed Hebrew מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם
entries.classical_he: כליהם — הקריאה הסטנדרטית של ה'מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם' החידתי
entries.saadia_en: their appointed-allotments — Saadia reads מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם as 'fated portions', from فرض 'to appoint, allot'
entries.saadia_he: מנותיהם הקצובות — רס״ג קורא 'מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם' כ'חלקים שנקצבו', מן فرض
entries.mechanism: The Hebrew hapax מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם is famously disputed (LXX renders 'their conspiracies', Ibn Ezra 'their swords'); Saadia derives it from a root meaning 'allotment, divinely-fixed share', rendering with فَرْض. This is a lexical-theological choice that softens the violence into 'their appointed portion'.

blau_dict.sense: فرضة 'an appointed/allotted portion' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 49:5 ('כלי חמס מכרתיהם' = פי אלאת אלצ'לם פרצ'תהמא).

entries.classical_en: Hebrew הוֹאַלְתִּי — 'I have undertaken / been so bold as to (speak)'
entries.classical_he: הוֹאַלְתִּי בלשון העברית — 'נטלתי על עצמי, ערבתי את לבי לדבר'
entries.saadia_en: Form IV أمعن — 'I have persisted / gone deep' in speaking
entries.mechanism: Saadia reads Abraham's diplomatic apology not as 'I dared to speak' (the volitional Hebrew הואלתי) but as 'I have persisted / gone in deep' (the intensive Arabic أمعن في الكلام). The shift moves Abraham's posture from boldness to persistence — closer to the rabbinic gloss of his repeated mercy-pleas.

blau_dict.sense: Form IV أمعن في 'to persist deep in, to go far in (an action)' — Blau records the JA usage citing Saadia on Gen 18:27 ('הואלתי לדבר' = אמענת פי אלכלאם).

entries.classical_en: Hebrew אוֹנ — 'virility, generative power' (the procreative reading)
entries.classical_he: אוֹן בלשון העברית — 'כוח גברי, כוח הזרע'
entries.saadia_en: Arabic نيل — 'acquisition, gain' (the economic-status reading)
entries.saadia_he: ניל בלשון הערבית — 'השגה, רווח, קניין' — קריאה כלכלית-מעמדית
entries.mechanism: Saadia recasts the biblical-Hebrew אוֹנ — usually read as generative strength — as Arabic نَيل ('what one gains, one's acquisition'). Jacob's blessing of Reuven shifts from a statement about virility to a statement about firstborn-economic priority. Blau treats the rendering under root نيل alongside the parallel נילי 'my gain'.

blau_dict.sense: نَيل 'acquisition, gain' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 49:3 ('כחי וראשית אוני' = וקותי ואוול נילי).

entries.classical_en: Hebrew אֹשֶׁר / אִשֵּׁר — 'happiness' / 'to call happy, congratulate'
entries.classical_he: אֹשֶׁר ואִשֵּׁר בלשון המקרא — 'אושר' ו'לקרוא מאושר'
entries.saadia_en: Arabic وصف — 'description, characterization' / Form I 'to describe, characterize (favorably)'
entries.mechanism: Saadia renders Leah's word-play אִשְּׁרוּנִי בָּנוֹת ('daughters have called me happy') with a verb of public characterization יצפני אלנסא ('women will describe/characterize me [favorably]'). The shift moves the inner state (happiness) outward into reputation — Asher as 'the one I am praised for'.

blau_dict.sense: وصف Form I 'to describe, characterize, extol' — Blau attests in the laudatory sense citing Saadia on Gen 30:13 ('באשרי כי אשרוני' = מן וצפי אן יצפני).

entries.classical_en: for the purpose of, in order that — JA equivalent of Hebrew לְמַעַן
entries.classical_he: לְמַעַן, על מנת ש- (תרגום ערבי-יהודי קבוע)
entries.saadia_en: in order that
entries.mechanism: Standard JA prepositional phrase: لـِ + قِبَل ('toward the matter that') renders biblical לְמַעַן (purpose); Blau notes the systematic equivalence.

blau_dict.sense: لقِبَل 'for the sake of, in order that' — Blau notes Saadia regularly renders biblical לְמַעַן with this JA phrase, citing Gen 37:22.

entries.classical_en: Hebrew וְיוֹכִיחוּ בֵּין שְׁנֵינוּ — 'let them decide between us' (subject unspecified)
entries.classical_he: וְיוֹכִיחוּ בֵּינֵינוּ — קריאה משפטית סתמית, ללא נושא מפורש
entries.saadia_en: Saadia names the disputed object — 'let them judge between us about the swap (אלבד'ל)' — the alleged misappropriation
entries.saadia_he: רס״ג מפרש את נושא ההכרעה: שיכריעו בינינו על החליפין/הגניבה
entries.mechanism: The Hebrew verse leaves the matter to be adjudicated implicit; Saadia supplies it. 'אלבד'ל' (the swap, the exchange) names the specific dispute — Laban's accusation that Jacob took his household gods. Saadia turns a generic juridical formula into a pointed reference to the underlying property claim.

blau_dict.sense: بدل 'exchange, swap, substitute' — Blau records the JA usage of بدل as a substantive for an exchange or substitution; here Saadia uses it to name the matter Laban wants adjudicated.

entries.classical_en: except (for), but for — JA preposition rendering biblical רַק
entries.classical_he: מלבד, חוץ מ-, אבל ל-
entries.saadia_en: except for
entries.mechanism: Standard JA preposition: عدا renders biblical-Hebrew רַק in the 'only, except' sense; Blau records the equivalence (with a note that the form blends عداه and فضلاً عنه).

blau_dict.sense: عدا 'except (for), but (for)' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 19:8 ('רק לאנשים האל אל תעשו' = עדא בהולאי אלקום לא תצנעו).

entries.classical_en: torch (high-register Arabic synonym for the common مشعل / شعلة)
entries.classical_he: לַפִּיד
entries.saadia_en: torch
entries.mechanism: High-register noun choice: Saadia preserves the biblical-Hebrew register of לַפִּיד (rare, elevated) by reaching for Arabic فليل rather than the prosaic مشعل; Blau records the equivalence with plural فلائل.

blau_dict.sense: فليل (pl. فلائل) 'torch' — Blau attests citing Saadia on Gen 15:17 ('ולפיד אש' = ופליל נאר) and the parallel rendering of לפידים at Ex 20:18.

entries.classical_en: winter (Hebrew-shaped usage) — biblical translators stretch خريف from 'autumn' to encompass 'winter/cold-season'
entries.classical_he: חֹרֶף — מתרגמי המקרא מותחים את 'כ'ריף' ('סתיו') להוראת חורף
entries.saadia_en: winter
entries.mechanism: Hebrew-shaped lexical extension: classical Arabic خريف means 'autumn', not 'winter', but biblical translators (Saadia included) extend it to render the Hebrew חֹרֶף — the cold-half of the year. Pairs with قيظ for קַיִץ in the same verse, completing the four-season frame.

blau_dict.sense: خريف 'winter' (under Hebrew influence; classical Arabic = 'autumn') — Blau attests in biblical translation traditions only, citing Saadia on Gen 8:22 and Ps 74:17 (קיץ וחוף = אלקיל ואלכ'ריף).

entries.classical_en: Form II denominative of سيد (master, lord) — "to make so. master/ruler" (post-classical; the standard sense of سيد in classical Arabic is the noun "lord", not a verbal action)
entries.classical_he: בנין שני דנומינטיבי מן سيد (אדון, שליט) — "להפוך מישהו לאדון/שליט" (פוסט-קלסי; המשמע הקלסי של سيد הוא שם-עצם "אדון" ולא פעולה)
entries.saadia_en: they shall make you ruler — Saadia recasts the Hebrew יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ ("your brothers shall praise you", from יד״ה which puns on Judah's name) as יסיידונך אכ'ותך ("your brothers shall make you ruler"). The acknowledgment in the blessing is reread as a political acclamation: the brothers don't celebrate Judah, they install him over themselves
entries.saadia_he: יִשְׁלִיטוּ אוֹתְךָ — סעדיה מתרגם את "יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ" של ברכת יהודה (מן השורש יד״ה שמשחק על שם יהודה) כ"יסיידונך אכ'ותך" ("אחיך ישליטו אותך עליהם"). ההודיה הופכת לאקלמציה פוליטית: האחים לא מהללים את יהודה אלא ממליכים אותו
entries.mechanism: interpretive paradigm shift: the Hebrew pun (יוֹדוּ↔יהודה) and the surface sense ("praise") are both jettisoned. Saadia commits to a political reading on which the Judah blessing is the constitutional charter for Davidic primacy among the tribes — and uses a denominative verb ("to make-ruler") that classical Arabic itself does not attest in this volitional sense. Blau glosses the JA verb explicitly as ישליטון

blau_dict.sense: Form II denominative of سيد (derived from سود ~ سيد): "to make so. master, lord / אדון, שליט" — Blau cites Saadia on Gen 49:8 directly: "יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ → יסיידונך אכ'ותך" and glosses as "ישליטון אחיך".

entries.classical_en: Form II of درق (with the prefix بـ in Blau's notation بدرق): "to escort, to accompany a traveller, to provide safe-conduct." Rare post-classical verb, related to درقة ("shield"); semantically very distinct from طرد ("to expel") which is the obvious lexical choice for the Hebrew וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ in this context
entries.classical_he: בנין שני של ד-ר-ק (לפי בלאו עם תחיליות בـ — بدرق): "ללוות, לתת בידי הולכי דרך הגנה וליווי". פועל פוסט-קלסי נדיר, קשור ל-درقة ("מגן"); רחוק סמנטית מטרד ("גרש") שהיא הבחירה הלקסיקלית הברורה לעברית "וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ" בהקשר זה
entries.saadia_en: they escorted him — Saadia renders Pharaoh's expulsion of Abram וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ אֹתוֹ וְאֶת-אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת-כָּל-אֲשֶׁר-לוֹ as פוכל עליה פרעון קומא וד'רקובה ("Pharaoh charged men with him and they escorted him"), softening the expulsion into a ceremonial dismissal. Dirinbourg emended to פבזרקו ("and they cast him out") to fit the harsher reading; Blau corrects this back to درق — Saadia genuinely wrote "escorted"
entries.saadia_he: וְלִוּוּ אוֹתוֹ — סעדיה מתרגם את גירוש אברם על-ידי פרעה ("וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ אֹתוֹ וְאֶת-אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת-כָּל-אֲשֶׁר-לוֹ") כ"פוכל עליה פרעון קומא וד'רקובה" ("פרעה הפקיד עליו אנשים והם ליווהו לדרך"), והופך את הגירוש לפרידה מכובדת. דירינבורג הגיה ל"פבזרקו" ("וְזָרְקוּ אוֹתוֹ") בעקבות הקריאה הקשה; בלאו מתקן בחזרה ל-درق — סעדיה אכן כתב "לִוּוּ"
entries.mechanism: interpretive: Pharaoh's send-off of Abram, which the Hebrew verb שׁ-ל-ח can read either as expulsion ("he sent away") or as escorted-dismissal ("he sent off with provision"), is committed by Saadia to the courteous reading. This dovetails with Saadia's wider rehabilitation of Pharaoh-of-Abram against Pharaoh-of-Moses — and stands directly opposed to the lectio facilior of the Samaritan tradition (واطلقوه, "and they released him") and Dirinbourg's emendation

blau_dict.sense: Form II with بـ: "to escort (a traveller), to provide safe-conduct / לִוָּה (נוֹסֵעַ, שַׁיָּרָה)" — Blau cites Saadia on Gen 12:20 directly as the canonical attestation, explicitly correcting Dirinbourg's emendation פבזרקו ("expelled") back to פבדרקו. The Samaritan tradition's lectio facilior واطلقوه ("released") further isolates Saadia's lexical choice as deliberate.

entries.classical_en: passive participle of متّع (Form II) "to give enjoyment, to grant pleasure" — "she who is given (over) for pleasure." Classical Arabic uses متعة for a temporary marriage contract (Shia jurisprudence) and the feminine participle as a regional term; never attested as a stable noun for cult-prostitute
entries.classical_he: בינוני פעול של متّع (בנין II) "לתת הנאה, להעניק תענוג" — "זו שנמסרה להנאה". בערבית הקלסית متعة היא חוזה נישואין זמני (משפט שיעי) והבינוני הנקבה הוא מונח אזורי; אינו מתועד כשם עצם יציב לכוהנת-זונה
entries.saadia_en: the temple-prostitute — Saadia renders the doubled Hebrew הַקְּדֵשָׁה ("the cult-prostitute," who Judah's friend Hirah asks the local men about, claiming to seek the woman Judah encountered) as אלממתעה ("the woman of pleasure-giving"). The choice of متّعة over the more neutral زانية (prostitute) commits Saadia to identifying קְדֵשָׁה as the cultic class specifically — not freelance prostitution but ritualized fertility-prostitution institutionalized at shrines
entries.saadia_he: הקדשה ("כוהנת-זונה") — סעדיה מתרגם את הצמד "הַקְּדֵשָׁה" (כאשר חירה הָעֲדֻלָּמִי שׁוֹאֵל את אנשי המקום על האישה ש"יהודה התעלה עליה") כ"אלממתעה" ("זו שלהנאה"). בחירת متّعة על פני הפועל הניטרלי زانية (זונה) מחייבת את סעדיה לזהות את "קדשה" כסיווג פולחני ספציפי — לא זנות חופשית אלא זנות פולחנית-פריונית קבועה בָּמְקוֹם הַקָּדוֹשׁ
entries.mechanism:
Lexical specification (anti-rabbinic / against the targumic neutralization), documented across a full cross-Pentateuchal arc that binds the NARRATIVE Tamar pericope (Gen 38:15, 21, 22) to the LEGISLATIVE prohibition (Deut 23:18). The Targumim and most medieval commentators render קְדֵשָׁה with a generic 'prostitute' word, effacing the cultic dimension. Saadia, working in an Islamic juristic-lexicographical milieu where متعة carries technical resonance (the Shia متعة-marriage contract), instead picks a term that names the cultic-utility category and deploys it as a stable terminus-technicus wherever the cult-prostitute appears.

NARRATIVE (Gen 38, Tamar): (1) Gen 38:15 (Heb וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לְזוֹנָה 'and he reckoned her a harlot' = וחסבהא ממתעה — Saadia reroutes even the generic Heb זוֹנָה through ממתעה, surfacing the cultic-prostitute category where the Hebrew uses the plain harlot-word); (2) Gen 38:21 (Heb אַיֵּה הַקְּדֵשָׁה 'where is the cult-prostitute' = אין אלממתעה — the anchor); (3) Gen 38:22 (Heb לֹא הָיְתָה בָזֶה קְדֵשָׁה = מא כאנת ההנא ממתעה).
